rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary treats ışâr as the plural of uşerâ, analogously to nifâs and nüfesâ.
rows.anchor: Ayn’ın kesriyle “ışâr”, ayn’ın zammı ve şîn’in fethiyle “uşerâ”nın cem‘idir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs called a she-camel uşerâ while she was ten months pregnant; such camels were among their most valuable possessions.
rows.anchor: Araplar on aylık gebe deveye doğuruncaya kadar bu nâmı verirler ve nazarlarında en kıymetli mallarıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Işâr denotes a herd of newly calved or nearly calving camels, precious animals requiring exceptional care.
rows.anchor: Bunların ta‘tîli ise çobansız, bakımsız mühmel bırakılıvermesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners abandon even their finest property amid the terrors of the approaching Resurrection, when wealth and children cannot avail except for a sound heart.
rows.anchor: sâhipleri böyle en nefis mallarını bile ihmal edip bırakırlar.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Some interpret the abandonment of the pregnant camels as a metaphor for clouds drying up and rain stopping; Arabs liken clouds to pregnant females, and the image also fits the moving of mountains.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin beyânına göre bazıları ta‘tîl-i

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Other interpreters take ışâr as cultivated land subject to tithe or tax, or as territories and homelands.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre bazıları da ziraat olunur; öşrü, vergisi alınır arazi, bazıları da diyar demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Kurtubî
rows.claim: Kurtubī reads the scene as a parable depicting the event's severity: in reality no such camels would be left unattended, but their owners would abandon them if they had them.
rows.anchor: Kurtubî demiştir ki: “Kelâm, şiddeti tasvir için temsil üzerinedir. Çünkü o zaman ne ışâr vardır ne ta‘tîl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the clauses use wāw rather than the sequencing fa, the abandonment may occur before the mountains move, as earthly earthquakes begin while camels, lands, and other prized property still exist.
rows.anchor: âyetler tertîbe delâlet eden fâ ile değil, vâv ile atfedilmiş olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vuhūsh are wild animals: the generic term for terrestrial creatures that do not associate with humans, opposite domesticated animals.
rows.anchor: “Vahş”, “vahşî” müfredinin ism-i cinsidir ki insana ünsiyet etmeyen berrî hayvana denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing with the valuable domestic camels sets tame against wild; the gathering therefore encompasses beasts of every kind.
rows.anchor: Işâra münasebeti, “ehlî” ile “yabânî”nin tekabülüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that fear makes animals forget their habitual fears and rush from their dens together, heedless of predators and human power, when the fire that drives people and animals appears before the first blast.
rows.anchor: Her taraftan istîlâ eden havf u dehşet içinde hayvânâtın öteden beri korkageldiği şeyleri unutarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the gathering as animals being brought together in death and destruction; the idiom “the year gathered them” means that famine destroyed them.
rows.anchor: Hayvânâtın haşri ölüm ve helâkte toplanmaları denilmiştir. Çünkü kıtlık olduğu yıl

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda and others are reported to interpret the gathering as animals being resurrected and assembled for requital.
rows.anchor: Katâde ve birtakımlarından rivayet olunduğu üzere haşr-i vuhûş hayvanların da kısas için ba‘s olunup mahşere toplanmalarıdır.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra has the Prophet say that rights will be restored, even the hornless sheep's right being taken from the horned sheep.
rows.anchor: Müslim ve Tirmizî’de Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki:

rows.speaker: Ahmed b. Hanbel
rows.claim: Aḥmad's version extends the requital report to an ant receiving its right from another ant.
rows.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel’in rivayetinde “ve hatta karınca karıncadan.”

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says every creature, even a mosquito, will be gathered for requital.
rows.anchor: Katâde de bu âyette demiştir ki: “Her şey hatta sivrisinek kısas için haşrolunacak.”

rows.speaker: Mutezile
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila say God resurrects all animals to compensate for pains caused by death, killing, and other harms; He may then preserve some in Paradise or annihilate them as reports say.
rows.anchor: Mutezile demiştir ki: Allah teâlâ o gün hayvânâtın hepsini haşredecek ki dünyada mevt, katl ve sâir suretle onlara ermiş olan elemlerin ivazını vermek için.

rows.speaker: Ashâbımız ehl-i sünnet
rows.claim: The Sunnis hold that nothing is owed to creatures as an entitlement from God; He will nevertheless gather the beasts, restore the hornless sheep's right, then command them to die.
rows.anchor: Ashâbımız ehl-i sünnete göre ise Allah teâlâ üzerine istihkak hükmüyle bir şey vâcib olmaz.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some deny that animals other than humans and jinn are gathered, since they are not morally accountable.
rows.anchor: Bazıları sekaleynden mâ‘adâsı mükellef olmadıkları için haşrolunmaz demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although al-Tirmidhī grades the report sound and fair, the author says it was not transmitted as an exegesis of this verse; its authenticity establishes divine justice without requiring that reading, though the verse may evoke it.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî hadise hasen sahih demiştir. Şu kadar ki o hadis bu âyetin tefsiri olarak vârid olmuş değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given its place between abandoned camels and the seas being set ablaze, the author prefers the first interpretation as an event during earthly upheavals rather than a post-resurrection gathering.
rows.anchor: Onun için birinci mâna müreccahtır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasjīr means heating a furnace with blazing fire and filling it.
rows.anchor: “Tescîr” alevli ateşle fırını[^31] kızdırmak ve doldurmak mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that volcanic fires erupt from the seas and their waters dry up.
rows.anchor: Birincisi, denizlerden volkan hâlinde ateşler çıkarak sularının[^32] çekilmesi

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhārī from al-Ḥasan says not a drop of water will remain.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de Hasan’dan bir katre su kalmayacak diye mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation reads tasjīr as filling the seas with fire.
rows.anchor: Birisi evvelki mâna gibi ateşle doldurulmuş olması

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujāhid is reported to read tasjīr as filling; the author explains this either as fire filling the seas or as their waters being split and poured over the earth like a single sea.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den rivayet edildiği üzere doldurmak mânasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative filling image is that the seas split open and spread across the earth like one sea, alongside earthquakes, volcanoes, and moving mountains.
rows.anchor: denizlerin yarılıp akıtılarak Arz’ın her tarafını bir deniz hâlinde istîlâ etmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says al-Bukhārī also transmits these three interpretations in summary.
rows.anchor: Bu üç mâna Buhârî’de de icmâlen menkuldür.

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers a possible derivation from sājūr, a dog's collar: tasjīr then metaphorically depicts the turbulent seas as restrained and controlled.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye tefsirinde mezkur olduğu üzere denilmiştir ki: “Tescîr”, “sâcûr”dan olmak muhtemildir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Âliye
rows.claim: Abū ʿĀliya divides the surah into six signs witnessed in this world, from the sun through the seas, and six belonging to the afterlife, from the souls being paired through Paradise being brought near.
rows.anchor: Abd b. Humeyd ve İbn Münzir Ebû Âliye’den rivayet etmişlerdir ki bu sûreden altı âyet dünyada ve insanlar bakarlarken, altısı da âhirettedir.

rows.speaker: Übey b. Ka‘b
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb reports that while people are in the markets the signs unfold: luminaries dim, mountains and earth quake, humans and jinn panic, beasts mingle, pregnant camels are neglected, seas ignite, earth splits, and a wind kills all.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebi’d-Dünya ve İbn Cerîr ve İbn Ebî Hâtim de Übey b. Ka‘b’dan şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir: Altı âyet kıyamet gününden evvel “nâs esvâkında iken”dir;

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the first six signs occur between the two blasts, and that this is what interpreters mean by saying they occur in this world.
rows.anchor: Bazıları “ilk altı iki nefha arasındadır, dünyada diyenlerin murâdı da budur” demişler

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Others say the first six unfold before the first blast and continue until the second; the author says this span must include the second blast too, since questioning occurs afterward.
rows.anchor: bazıları da “onlar nefha-i ûlâdan önce, mâba‘di nefha-i sâniyeye kadardır” demişler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author construes the latter view's endpoint as including the second blast, because questioning takes place later.
rows.anchor: Çünkü sual sonradır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nufūs is the plural of nafs, which can mean a self or person as well as a soul or spirit.
rows.anchor: “Nefs” de zât ve rûh mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazwīj can mean joining each person to a counterpart, equal, or analogue, and thus arranging people into classes or uniting them.
rows.anchor: “Tezvîc” de eşi eşe, dengi denge, emsâl ve akrânı birbirine zam ve ilhak edip bir yere getirmek

rows.speaker: Ömer
rows.claim: ʿUmar explains the pairing as each person being joined to a counterpart from the people of Paradise or Hell, and recites 37:22.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de “Hazret-i Ömer ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ ehl-i cennet ve ehl-i nârdan nazîri ile tezvic olunur” dedi

rows.speaker: نعمان بن بشير
rows.claim: Nuʿmān b. Bashīr reports hearing ʿUmar preach and explain the pairing as groups destined for Paradise and groups destined for Hell.
rows.anchor: Numan b. Beşir radıyallâhu anh demiştir ki: ‘Ömer b. el-Hattâb radıyallâhu anh hutbe okuyordu

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet explains the paired groups as each person being gathered with the people whose deeds resemble his own.
rows.anchor: Yine Numan b. Beşir merfû‘an Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den rivayet ederek demiştir ki: “وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ durebâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Durebā is the plural of ḍarīb, meaning a class or likeness; the pairing therefore sorts people with those whose deeds they resemble, good with good and bad with bad.
rows.anchor: “Durebâ”, sınıf ve şebîh mânasına “darîb”in cem‘i

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the verse as the time when people are in three groups.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan da: وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ nâs ezvâc-ı selâse olduğu vakit.

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says each person is joined to his faction.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan: Her kişi şî‘asına ilhak olunduğu vakit.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says people's peers are gathered together.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Nâs içinde emsal birbirleriyle cem‘olunduğu vakit.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says each person is joined to his own faction, Jews with Jews and Christians with Christians.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den: Her insan kendi şî‘asına: Yehûd Yehûda, Nasârâ Nasârâya ilhak edildiği vakit.

rows.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Rabīʿ b. Khuthaym says each person is resurrected together with the person of his deeds.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Huseym’den[^47]: Herkes sâhib-ameliyle haşrolunur:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, people are summoned class by class with their good or evil leaders and those like them, then divided in the great court into the people of the right and left and the two final destinations.
rows.anchor: insanların hayr u şer amelde metbû‘ları ve birbirlerine benzerleri ile sınıf sınıf, fevc fevc mahşere davet olunup mahkeme-i kübrâda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grouping also includes each soul standing with its companion or adversary, as described in the verse about every soul arriving with a driver and witness.
rows.anchor: bunda sûre-i Kāf’ta geçen وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌۭ وَشَهِيدٌۭ [50/21] mazmûnu: Dostun dost ile, hasmın hasım ile

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some infer that believers are paired with their wives and houris in Paradise while disbelievers are joined to devils in Hell.
rows.anchor: tâbirinden[^50] bazıları mü’minlerin cennette zevceleri ve huriler ile tezvicleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that as the primary sense: since Paradise is only brought near in the next verse, this pairing is the prior sorting of classes destined for Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: bu henüz cennet ve cehenneme girilmeden önceki tasnif ve tefrîki anlattığı için

rows.speaker: İkrime, Dahhâk ve Şa‘bî
rows.claim: ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Shaʿbī interpret nufūs as spirits being returned to bodies at the second blast and resurrection.
rows.anchor: İkrime, Dahhâk ve Şa‘bî’den rivayet olunduğu üzere “nüfûs” ervâh mânasına olarak ervâhın ecsâda iade olunup birleştirildiği vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both interpretations concern the resurrection's second phase, but the first has stronger transmission and a broader meaning.
rows.anchor: rivayet itibariyle evvelki daha kuvvetli ve mâna itibariyle de daha şümullüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing prepares both sides for the great court and is tied to questioning and accounting, which the following scene makes explicit.
rows.anchor: Bunun bilhassa tarafeyni mahkeme-i kübrâya ihzar mânasında sual ve hesab ile alâkadar olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawʾūda is a girl buried alive, from waʾd, a term associated with pressing down or burying; this was a shameful pre-Islamic Arab custom.
rows.anchor: “Mev’ûde” (مَوْئُودَه): Küçükken diri olarak gömülüp öldürülen kızcağız demektir ki “ve’d”den müştaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs buried daughters from fear of shame or poverty and inability to provide; some also acted on the belief that angels were God's daughters and that girls should be joined to them.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin beyan ettikleri vechile câhiliye Araplarında bu çirkin âdet şâyi‘idi ve bunu türlü türlü yaparlardı.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alūsī reports that a girl spared from killing could be dressed in a wool or hair cloak and made to tend sheep or camels in the desert; those choosing to kill her might lure a six-year-old to a pit and bury her, or throw a newborn girl into a pit while keeping a boy.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin beyânına göre bir değil, birçokları zikretmiştir ki:

rows.speaker: Kāmûs şârihi
rows.claim: The Kāmūs commentator says Arabs buried daughters through fear of hunger or shame, and some also buried sons from fear of hunger; the verse was revealed about this practice.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs şârihi der ki: “Câhiliyede Araplar kız evlâdını açlık veya âr gelme korkusundan kabre defnederlerdi

rows.speaker: Abduh
rows.claim: Muḥammad ʿAbduh laments the killing of innocent girls for poverty or shame and praises Islam for replacing cruelty with mercy and eradicating the custom as a boon to humanity.
rows.anchor: Mısır müftîsi Abduh burada şöyle demiştir: “Bak şu kasvete, şu katı yürekliliğe

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Qays b. ʿĀṣim told the Prophet he had buried eight daughters in the pre-Islamic period; the Prophet ordered one slave to be freed for each, or one sacrificial camel if he owned camels.
rows.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ‘her birinden bir rakabe âzâd et’ buyurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Islam wipes away what preceded it, the command to free a slave or sacrifice a camel is recommended rather than a condition for valid repentance; it also underscores the enormity of infanticide.
rows.anchor: اَلإِْسْلاَمُ يَجُبُّ مَا قـَبـْلَهُ İslâm mâkablini keser atar”

rows.speaker: Ferezdak
rows.claim: Ferezdak boasts that his grandfather Saʿṣaʿa b. Nājiya protected girls who were to be buried and brought buried infants back to life, evidence that some Arabs abhorred the practice.
rows.anchor: Ferezdak şu beytinde وجَدِّي الّذِي مَنَعَ الْوَائِدَاتِ وَأَحْيَا الْوَئِيدَ فَلَمْ تُوئَدِ

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Saʿṣaʿa told the Prophet he had rescued 360 buried girls, buying each with two ten-month camels; the Prophet said he would be rewarded because God had bestowed Islam on him.
rows.anchor: Taberânî, müşârün ileyh [5605] Sa‘sa‘a’dan şöyle rivayet eylemiştir:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because infanticide is killing one's children, most often from fear of poverty, the Qurʾān forbids it in several passages, including commands not to kill children from want or fear of want and the women's pledge.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i En‘âm’da وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُم مِّنْ إِمْلَٰقٍۢ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These prohibitions concern deliberate killing of one's offspring by any means, not only burial alive; intentional abortion is likewise killing one's child and a grave homicide.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetlere nazaran yalnız gömmek suretiyle değil, herhangi bir suretle olursa olsun evlâdını amden öldürmek de böyle büyük bir cinayettir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report from Khidāma bt. Wahb says the Prophet called coitus interruptus “hidden infanticide.”
rows.anchor: Huzâme binti Vehb’den rivayet etmişlerdir ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ne azilden sual olundu, “ذلِكَ الْوَأْدُ الْخَفِيُّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some jurists regarded coitus interruptus as forbidden, the established legal view is that it is disliked because it can be misused as a means of cutting off offspring.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı azlin de hurmetine kāil olanlar olmuşsa da fıkıhta kerâhet olması tahkik olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If withdrawal is hidden infanticide, aborting formed fetuses or killing newborn children is plainly a forbidden grave crime, whether done directly or by causing it.
rows.anchor: Azil, ve’d-i hafî olunca hilkati tebeyyün etmiş ceninlerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victim, presumed to lack a protector, is questioned before the killer to expose the gravity of unjustly killing her and to make the murderer feel the force of his defeat before the innocent.
rows.anchor: bunun evvelâ kātile değil, katlolunan masum kızcağıza sorulacağı anlatılarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking the victim rather than the perpetrator why she was killed is a severe reproach, called tabkīt: it makes the killer recognize his injustice and inability to defend himself before God.
rows.anchor: şiddetli bir ihtar ve târiz vardır ki buna “tebkît” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioning of Jesus about whether he told people to worship him and his mother similarly reproaches the Christians.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ muvacehesinde Hazret-i Îsâ’ya ءَأَنتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِى وَأُمِّىَ إِلَٰهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets may be the books of deeds, opened for reckoning, or records distributed after the accounting as an announcement of the verdict.
rows.anchor: Burada iki nevi suhuf zikredilmiştir: Birisi amel defterleridir ki bunların neşri hesab için açılmaları demektir.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a person's record is folded when he dies, then opened on Resurrection Day and used for his account.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir’in İbn Cüreyc’den rivayet ettiği vechile “insan ölünce sahîfesi dürülür, sonra kıyamet günü açılır, ona göre hesâbı görülür”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second interpretation is that the sheets are spread and distributed after the reckoning, as in the record given in 69:19; some hadith call this the flying of the pages.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Hâkka’da فَاَمَّا مَنْ اُو۫تِيَ كِتَابَهُ’de [69/19] dahi geçtiği vechile hesâbın rü’yetinden sonra i‘lâm gibi neşr ü tevzî‘olunacak sahîfelerdir

rows.speaker: مرثد بن وداعة
rows.claim: Mersed b. Wadāʿa reports that pages fly from beneath the Throne on Resurrection Day: the believer's page reaches him in the high Garden and the unbeliever's in scorching wind and boiling water.
rows.anchor: Mersed b. Vedâ‘a’dan mervîdir ki “Kıyamet günü olunca Arş’ın tahtından sahîfeler uçuşur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first reading, the books opened for reckoning; the following surah's description of noble recording angels explains it, and this is the day when all deeds are exposed.
rows.anchor: Burada birincisi daha akrebdir.
